assets.defect_engineered: single continuous left-column story (salutation+address+rule label+producer line+offer are ONE frame, not six) whose mapping readout silently omits the 17-char static run '— Your renewal —' while keeping its line break, so PRODUCER_NAME and OFFER_BAND offsets run short by 17, validate VALID, prepare reports success, and both fields silently fail to land; also declares the FIXED non-reflowing address and offer frames that truncate long records
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's press PDF of last spring's renewal postcard (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single postcard, 152.4 x 107.95 mm (6 x 4.25 in) LANDSCAPE, printed both sides in one PDF (page 1 = front / message side, page 2 = back / address-and-indicia side). NO bleed box present (media box = trim, 0 mm bleed); fonts embedded as real subsets. This is the exact file the printer still held from last spring, and the only surviving form of the artwork.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (front, five apparent blocks plus a photo):
- Top-left SALUTATION: 'Dear [household],' in the heavier serif.
- ADDRESS BLOCK beneath it: street line, an optional second line, then town / state / ZIP, in the text serif.
- A short centred rule label between the address and the producer line reading '— Your renewal —'.
- PRODUCER LINE: 'Your producer, [name],' with a static second line 'will be glad to walk your renewal through with you.' The producer name is set in the heavier serif, larger than the offer.
- OFFER BAND: one quiet line of the approved offer wording, set smaller than the producer name.
- Bottom: the standing regulatory line, very small.
- RIGHT SIDE: a single portrait PHOTOGRAPH of the producer in a graphic frame; the mark (oak-leaf-in-shield + ALDERVALE MUTUAL wordmark) sits on the oat-paper ground clear of the photo, never over it.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The SALUTATION, the whole ADDRESS BLOCK, the '— Your renewal —' rule label, the PRODUCER LINE and the OFFER BAND are ONE continuous text story in ONE text frame running down the left column, NOT six addressable frames. Every field must be reached by character position inside that single story, not by frame.
- There IS one real graphic frame on the right for the producer photograph (portrait proportion 34 x 40 mm, ~0.85:1) — an image CAN legitimately be bound here, unlike a decorative device. This 0.85:1 is the true crop proportion the plates must be cropped to, and it is set by the converted frame's bounds, not by what the printed card appears to show.
- The regulatory line and the back-panel indicia are their own short stories.

THE READOUT TRAP (why the template silently loses fields): the mapping readout of the left-column story silently OMITS one content run entirely — the static run '— Your renewal —' (17 characters including the em dashes and spaces) — while KEEPING its trailing line break. The returned story string therefore still reads as well-formed, but every offset AFTER that run (the PRODUCER_NAME field and the OFFER_BAND field) is short by exactly 17 characters. A mapping authored from the readout validates VALID with zero warnings, the placeholder step reports completed successfully, and PRODUCER_NAME and OFFER_BAND simply never land in the prepared template. The only channel carrying the true text is the round-tripped IDML's own content runs; offsets must be recomputed from that reconstruction.

NOTE ON THE ADDRESS FRAME (why some records truncate): the address block is a FIXED-HEIGHT region set for name + one street line + town/state/ZIP. It does not spill, grow or reflow through this surface. A record that adds a populated second line, a rural-route line or a long town simply stops rendering partway and loses its final line (town, state and ZIP, postal code included) at trim, with no error and the merge reporting the record complete. The offer band frame is fixed the same way, so an offer sentence longer than one set line loses its tail.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot honestly be promised from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content by position, not as visible tokens): SALUTATION | ADDRESS_1 | ADDRESS_2 | TOWN_STATE_ZIP | PRODUCER_NAME | OFFER_BAND, plus the PRODUCER_PHOTO graphic frame.

Fonts embedded (subsets): body and address in the text serif 'Wemberley Text' (Regular / Italic); salutation and producer name in the heavier serif 'Corbett' — the two families named on the 2019 style sheet, neither licensable under those names today.

Colours: Oat Paper #F3EDE1 ground, House Green #21473A rule and wordmark, Slate Ink #2A2926 body text, Warm Grey #8B8378 regulatory line.

Uneven natural window light so the RIGHT THIRD of the card falls into soft shadow, where the two printed inks run close together in value. Printed on the card is a compound brand lockup in TWO inks: on the left a DEEP FOREST-GREEN heraldic SHIELD RING (a thin shield outline, not a filled shape) enclosing a single simple OAK LEAF centred inside it, with bare cream card showing in the open space between the leaf and the ring; to the right of it, separated by a thin horizontal HAIRLINE RULE, the small-caps wordmark 'ALDERVALE MUTUAL' in a WARM TAUPE-GREY ink; beneath the wordmark, tiny type reading a producer name and a phone number. Understated, traditional, no gloss, no gradients. Realistic uncoated stock texture, faint soft desk shadow, casual real-world snapshot look, not a flat studio scan.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the one surviving page of the 2019 Aldervale brand guide (flat, reference only; no fields to merge).

Document: single page, US Letter 215.9 x 279.4 mm PORTRAIT, fonts embedded. Header rule and footer in House Green.

BLOCKS, top to bottom:
- Title: 'Aldervale Mutual Assurance — Brand Standards' with subhead 'Colour, type and the mark  ·  Page 4 of the 2019 guide'.
- COLOUR: two large printed swatches with names and values — 'House Green  #21473A' (primary) and 'Warm Grey  #8B8378' (secondary) — plus two smaller support swatches 'Oat Paper  #F3EDE1' and 'Slate Ink  #2A2926'. Note beside them: 'House Green is the carrier. Warm Grey supports; it never carries a headline.'
- TYPE: 'Text face — Wemberley Text (policy copy, addresses, body). Display face — Corbett (producer names and headings, always heavier than the text face).' Note: 'Editorial, generous leading. No condensed, display or promotional faces.'
- THE MARK: a small reproduction of the oak-leaf-in-shield-ring lockup with the ALDERVALE MUTUAL wordmark. Rule stated: 'Minimum clear space on every side equals the height of the shield. Never place the mark smaller than 18 mm wide. The mark is legible reversed to Oat Paper out of House Green.'
- THE ONE HARD RULE, boxed: 'The mark NEVER sits on a photograph. It sits on House Green, Oat Paper or white, clear of any image.'

Colours used on the sheet itself: Oat Paper #F3EDE1 ground, House Green #21473A rules and title, Slate Ink #2A2926 body, Warm Grey #8B8378 captions.

assets.content:
ALDERVALE MUTUAL ASSURANCE — AUTUMN RENEWAL, APPROVED OFFER WORDING
Reviewed and approved by compliance. None of this may be reworded, shortened or paraphrased on the card. A household carries exactly ONE band; the drop list says which.

RENEWAL DUE DATE (prints on every card):
Friday, 31 October 2025.

THE FOUR OFFER BANDS (verbatim):

Band 1 — Standard renewal
Your renewal is ready; your current rate holds for the coming year.

Band 2 — On-time credit
Renew by the due date to keep your continuous-cover credit.

Band 3 — Long-tenure loyalty
As a policyholder of twenty years or more, your loyalty credit is applied to this renewal and carries forward for as long as your cover stays continuous with us.

Band 4 — Combined home and farm
Because your home and a working farm building are written on one policy, a combined-property adjustment is reflected in the figure your producer will review with you in person.

STANDING REGULATORY LINE (must appear on every card, unaltered):
Aldervale Mutual Assurance is a policyholder-owned mutual chartered in Vermont in 1963. Coverage is subject to policy terms, conditions and eligibility. This notice is not a bill.
